pr_title: Don't call EVP_fetchbyname if provider options used.
pr_body:
This is an attempt to fix #15372.  If any provider flags are specified, only call `EVP_fetch`

Everything passes except the CMS tests.  I am not surprised. :)  I would also appreciate help, maybe from @ddvo once he's done hleping fix NonStop :)
pr_comments: Hmmm, there are parts of CMS that still requires the presence of legacy structures (most of all a EVP_PKEY_ASN1_METHOD).  It's a tough cookie.  I've dealt quite a bit with those parts before, I can have another look to see what corner case you hit this time...

Actually, it seems that the CMS issue isn't so much about CMS, but about NULL being used for libctx and propq in opt_md_silent() and op_cipher_silent().  The best way would be to add those as arguments to opt_md, opt_cipher, etc, and pass them down for the apps.
@richsalz, I just pushed a commit, which seems to fix the CMS problem, at least when I'm testing on my machine

What made the CMS test an issue was actually this:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/06621ba387f8d45e0c273f77f18573eb52cd66b8/test/recipes/80-test_cms.t#L60

That's an environment that puts the apps an a bit of a special circumstance, where the default library context only has the NULL provider loaded, and all useful providers are placed in a separate and explicitly created library context.
That's fine, but I have to ask again, *why don't we **also** test normal circumstances, such as the default (NULL) library context being used*?  @openssl!
Happy to have you finish this off.
This should have gone into the beta :(
I can pick this up again if there's interest, but there doesn't seem to be much interest.  @levitte, @t8m, @paulidale ?  Or one of you just close it.
Closing as #16022 seems to be the replacement.

issue_context.title: Too aggressive error suppressing
issue_context.body:
Before #15371 is merged, when the digest was not found, there was no relevant output in the STDERR.
I suppose we have too aggressive error suppression somewhere in the EVP_SignInit* stuf

The command 
```
openssl dgst -d -hmac key data.txt
```
doesn't print any relevant error message though the `ERR_print_errors` is called.
comments: How should we label this issue to be triaged?

> How should we label this issue to be triaged?

Just add the "triaged: bug" label to say its been triaged by a committer but don't add the "OTC evaluated" label until OTC have looked at it. If you think its important to look at soon then add it to the beta 1 milestone (which I see you have done).
The fact is that we have *lots* of places in the provider code where we just return 0 or NULL with no error reporting whatsoever.  It's not error suppression, it's *lack of error reports*
I think we have both cases really. Don't know what exactly happens here.

Is there something we can do in the apps to ensure that all specified providers are loaded, via an API? This is something that https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/master/apps/dgst.c#L232 was intended to handle. But maybe that's not the problem?

> Is there something we can do in the apps to ensure that all specified providers are loaded, via an API?

Yes

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/340cf8759f904859e609cecf4315b7cb50cde561/include/openssl/provider.h#L24

When it comes to the apps, there's the config file, but it's harder to get errors that way
*Some* apps have a `-provider` flag, which I believe end up calling `OSSL_PROVIDER_load()`

Okay, let me be a bit more verbose.

The -provider_path, -provider, and -prop_query flags are handled by common code, in https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/340cf8759f904859e609cecf4315b7cb50cde561/apps/lib/app_provider.c  Those functions *seem* to load and check the provider right away. Are they doing that?  If they are, then my question is why doesn't the check in https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/master/apps/dgst.c#L232 do the right thing?

Hmmm, you're right that `opt_md()` doesn't use any propq:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/2ed0a45a65b0df10648a4c11d365e2e1ebb1e697/apps/lib/opt.c#L397-L419
So should `opt_md` use the app_propq?  And similar for `opt_cipher`?

... and the next question is also, if either the app propq or library context is non-NULL, or a default propq is set, should `EVP_get_digestbyname()` be called at all?

This discussion sounds like someone should raise an issue, btw

I don't know if a discussion is needed.  If you specify query and or providers and or libraries, then call the evp-get-by-name routine seems wrong.  See #15414 which does that.  But it breaks the CMS tests.

> The command
> 
> ```
> openssl dgst -d -hmac key data.txt
> ```
> 
> doesn't print any relevant error message though the `ERR_print_errors` is called.

I just had a related issue with **external-tests** using the gost engine, see https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/12095#issuecomment-846111317
I'm afraid it's a different problem. GOST engine is rather picky to console output, but here it looks like we have no errors on stack.

This is slated for 3.0 but it is not clear to me what needs to be done.  Can somebody provide some clarification?

The lack of libctx/propq was covered in #15687
The EVP_fetchbyname() PR #15414 seems to have stalled, does this need to be kicked along?

@paulidale could you please rollback the changes from #15371 and test if the relevant information is present in stderr (meaning that the error was put into the stack)? The original bug report was about that.

Without the changes in #15371 I just get the message _Error setting context_.  With the changes the MAC is computed.

Ths doesn't appear to be error suppression, rather it looks like a failure case isn't being handled.  I'll put a _no defualt digest_ in place.  I don't think that #15414 will fix this, it's a call to `evp_keymgmt_util_get_deflt_digest_name()` not finding a digest that's causing the issue.
`Error setting context` is an app-level error, isn't it? We should also get a library error. Yes, it could be just omitted by an accident. I also don't think that #15414 fix it.
#16015 just might :grinning:
I first did #15414 but then @levitte did some work on it and I turned it over to him.  Maybe he forgot that I did that. :)

My last comment in #15414 is "I don't agree with the solution any longer"

Details here: https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/15414#pullrequestreview-680893727

review_comments:
Since you now call `opt_md()` always with `app_get0_libctx()`,
why not simply make the libctx implicit, moving  `app_get0_libctx()` into `opt_md()`?

... because the test programs use opt.c but not all the rest of libapps, and must certainly not apps.c, as that comes with contradicting baggage.  #15342 is an effort to clean up libapps and make it easier to use for the test programs, and would essentially be required to do what you propose.  However, we're too close to beta1 for that effort, it's been rightfully postponed to post-3.0.0.

So this is a functional compromise that makes things work without having to refactor all of libapps.

I don't understand this, since `opt_md()` is used only in rather few places -
```
fgrep 'opt_md(' -r apps test
```
yields
```
apps/dgst.c:        if (!opt_md(digestname, &md))
apps/ocsp.c:            if (!opt_md(opt_arg(), &resp_certid_md))
apps/ocsp.c:            if (!opt_md(opt_unknown(), &cert_id_md))
apps/ocsp.c:        if (!opt_md(respdigname, &rsign_md))
apps/smime.c:        if (!opt_md(digestname, &sign_md))
apps/include/opt.h:int opt_md(const char *name, EVP_MD **mdp);
apps/lib/opt.c:int opt_md(const char *name, EVP_MD **mdp)
apps/crl.c:        if (!opt_md(digestname, &digest))
apps/pkcs12.c:            if (!opt_md(macalg, &macmd))
apps/cms.c:        if (!opt_md(digestname, &sign_md))
apps/ts.c:        if (!opt_md(digestname, &md))
apps/storeutl.c:        if (!opt_md(digestname, &digest))
apps/enc.c:        if (!opt_md(digestname, &dgst))
```
and AFAICS by this PR all uses take `app_get0_libctx()` (and not NULL) as argument.

If you move `app_get0_libctx()` into `opt_md()`, but not into `opt_md_silent()`, 
you still have the freedom to use NULL libctx via `opt_md_silent()`,
while the existing calls to `opt_md()` apparently then do not need to be changed.

That's not where the problem is.  The problem is that `app_get0_libctx()` and `app_get0_propq()` are defined in `apps/lib/apps.c`.  So, test programs would therefore need to have that as a source as well.  However, that sucks in a number of other symbols (functions) that test programs define their own variant of, and we get a number of symbol clashes when linking.

Of course, we could move `app_get0_libctx()` and `app_get0_propq()` to a separate source file.  However, they in turn depend on things like bio_err, bio_out and whatnot.  It rapidly becomes a mess to deal with.

Look, *you're welcome to try and see for yourself*, but be warned that it's not a small effort to deal with.
I'm choosing a route that *works* and is the least amount of effort.
Ah, now I understand the problem - thanks.

Still it would be possible to avoid adding `app_get0_libctx()` and `app_get0_propq()` to each and every call of `opt_md()` and `opt_cipher()` in the apps: by introducing intermediate `app_md()` and `app_cipher()` that take over this tedious job.
... and where would you place those?

In `apps.h`, for instance like this:
```
#define app_md(n, d) opt_md(app_get0_libctx(), n, app_get0_propq(), d)
#define app_cipher(n, c) opt_cipher(app_get0_libctx(), n, app_get0_propq(), c)
```

I think that defining the `app_md` macros to just add arguments is wrong for a couple of reasons:
- @levitte already did the work to add them to the calls
- Since `opt_` is intended primarily as "option parsing for the application," creating a new prefix `app_` that wraps the `opt_` function is very confusing.

In other words, this adds more work (undo the changes already done), and add new macros to avoid the changes that result in more confusing code.  You could mitigate the confusion by having  big block comment explaining why `app_md` exists, but that still doesn't change the fact that things work now.
Looking back, I find this solution a bit weird.  What happens if someone uses *both* `-provider` and `-engine`?  That's a valid combination, they don't exclude each other!
based on the documentation in this PR, it would seem that it would be an error to have both engine and providers.
In that case, I would say that this PR isn't quite right.

> Not sure why the counter is needed... I would have expected something like this:

It's really a flag, but I just did ++ instead of `= 1`  And it's a function because as you pointed out elsewhere, sharing global variables is messy.  More importantly, if there are config files loaded that set default, I wasn't sure about what would happen.  (The whole interaction of libctx and default providers is murky to me.)

Finally, I didn't want to set the libctx/propq as local variables because an errors woudl be outside the error stack clearing from the `set-mark` function.
